Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The failing test checks the cross product of two very large vectors that are almost collinear. The current bug report says the cross product implementation uses the naive formulas for each coordinate of the cross product: (y1 z2 - y2 z1, z1 x2 - x1 z2, x1 y2 - y1 x2). This naive approach is sensitive to numerical cancellation when vectors are almost collinear and very large.

Looking at the code snippet for Vector3D.crossProduct(Vector3D, Vector3D), we see the method comments mention sophisticated approaches to mitigate cancellation errors, including rescaling vectors, preconditioning, and using a vector v3 = v1 - rho v2 with a chosen rho to compute without loss of precision. It also references Kahan's paper on computing cross products with improved numerical stability.

However, the actual implementation code on line 473 just returns the naive cross product formula using the inputs v1 and v2 directly, without applying any of the described scaling or preconditioning steps. This causes numerical cancellation issues when the input vectors are large and nearly collinear.

Thus the test fails because the class documentation and comments indicate an intended numerical improvement that is not implemented in the code. The naive formula is not accurate under the tested conditions and produces the wrong cross product vector.

The crossProduct method in Vector3D currently returns the naive cross product formula instead of applying the intended numerical stability improvements mentioned in the comments, like rescaling vectors and preconditioning with a carefully chosen rho. This leads to floating point cancellation errors and incorrect results for very large and nearly collinear vectors, as demonstrated by the failing test.

The comments describe a more stable approach, but the implementation does not follow it.

The failing test explicitly shows the issue by using vectors with very large and close coordinates, and the naive formula returns a slightly wrong cross product vector.

This is the root cause of the failure.
